On this page

# What is Prismatic?

If you're a software company that sells to businesses (you're a B2B SaaS), chances are, you're not the only software vendor your customers use. Your customers buy software from you, and a bunch of other vendors. And, they naturally expect that the data in your system syncs with data they store in the other apps and services they use.

Meaning you've gotta build integrations that sync data between your app and the other apps your customers use.

Doing it all yourself is time-consuming. There are a TON of things you need to account for beyond writing some code that gets data from point A to point B.

With Prismatic, you provide the integration logic (either through our low-code designer or code-native SDK), and we provide the infrastructure that integrations need to run - things like a configuration experience, webhooks, OAuth 2.0, compute, CI/CD deployment, logging, monitoring, alerting... the list goes on.

## How do I build integrations?​

You have three options for building integrations:

  1. Your developers can build workflows and design a configuration experience using Prismatic's TypeScript SDK. Dev tools like Prismatic's [VSCode extension](/docs/dev-tools/vscode-extension/) and [MCP Dev Server](/docs/dev-tools/prism-mcp/) expedite the development process.
  2. Prismatic's **low-code designer** lets both developers and technical non-developers design workflows and a configuration wizard experience, and package them together into a productized integration.
  3. Your customers can build workflows for themselves within your app when you embed the [Workflow Builder](/docs/embed/workflow-builder/), and your customers can leverage [Prismatic's AI co-pilot](https://prismatic.io/blog/introducing-ai-copilot-for-embedded-workflow-builder/) to build quickly.



## What apps can I integrate with?​

Prismatic offers a library of hundreds of [built-in connectors](/docs/components/) for common third-party apps. But, you're not limited to our library. You can build your own [custom connector](/docs/custom-connectors/) for your own app and niche, industry-specific apps.

If the app has a web-based API, or if there's a Node.js library that supports it (e.g. database, SFTP, LDAP, etc), you can integrate with it.

# Prismatic Docs

> Prismatic is the integration platform for B2B SaaS companies, enabling them to build and manage integrations with ease. These docs provide comprehensive guides, tutorials, and API references to help developers create low-code and code-native integrations using Prismatic's platform.


## Documentation

- [Building a Custom MCP Flow Server](https://prismatic.io/docs/ai/custom-mcp-server.md): Build your own MCP server that invokes Prismatic agent flows
- [Data Enrichment with AI](https://prismatic.io/docs/ai/data-enrichment.md): Learn how to use AI to enrich data going through your flows
- [Flow Invocation Schemas](https://prismatic.io/docs/ai/flow-invocation-schema.md): Declare how a flow should be called by AI agents
- [MCP Endpoints](https://prismatic.io/docs/ai/mcp-endpoints.md): MCP endpoint URLs for Prismatic's hosted MCP flow server, scoped by region, integration, and instance
- [Prismatic's MCP Flow Server](https://prismatic.io/docs/ai/model-context-protocol.md): Build a model context protocol (MCP) server that consumes agent flows
- [Documentation for LLMs](https://prismatic.io/docs/ai/prismatic-docs.md): Prismatic provides documentation optimized for large language models (LLMs).
- [Test Using Common MCP Clients](https://prismatic.io/docs/ai/test-mcp-clients.md): Test your agent flows using common MCP clients like Claude Desktop, Claude Code, or Cursor

### Build Integrations

- [What are Productized Integrations?](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations.md): Build integrations as core product features with self-service deployment for better customer retention and stickiness.
- [Connections Overview](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections.md): Add connections to third-party APIs within your config wizard
- [Customer Connections](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/integration-agnostic-connections/customer-activated.md): Connections that customers activate that can be used in one or more integrations
- [Organization (Customer) Connections](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/integration-agnostic-connections/org-activated-customer.md): Connections that organizations activate on behalf of customers
- [Organization (Global) Connections](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/integration-agnostic-connections/org-activated-global.md): Connections that organizations activate and are shared by multiple customers
- [Integration-Scoped Connections](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/integration-specific.md): Connections that are used in a single integration
- [Managing Connections](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/managing.md): Learn how to manage your connections in the Integrations section of the dashboard.
- [What is OAuth 2.0?](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/oauth2.md): Connect to third-party applications with OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials or Auth Code flow
- [OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Grant Type](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/oauth2/authorization-code-grant-type.md): The authorization code grant type lets users grant permission to you to third-party applications
- [OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Grant Type](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/oauth2/client-credentials-grant-type.md): Client credentials, often called M2M, lets two systems authenticate with one another
- [Custom OAuth 2.0 Redirects](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/oauth2/custom-redirects.md): Redirect your users to a custom page of your choosing after completing OAuth
- [OAuth 2.0 Password Grant Type](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/oauth2/password-grant-type.md): Here, we'll cover the less common form of OAuth 2.0
- [Troubleshooting OAuth 2.0 Connections](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/oauth2/troubleshooting.md): Identify issues with OAuth 2.0 connections
- [On-Prem Agent](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/on-prem-agent.md): Connect to resources like databases or file storage systems that are not accessible from the public internet.
- [Support On-Prem Connections in Custom Connectors](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/on-prem-agent/custom-connectors.md): Add on-prem connection support to your custom connectors for connecting to private network resources
- [On-Prem Databases Requiring Client Libraries or Drivers](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/on-prem-agent/databases-with-client-libraries.md): Databases like IBM DB2 require additional client libraries or drivers to connect to them.
- [On-Prem Agent on Windows](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/on-prem-agent/on-prem-agent-windows.md): Run the on-prem container on a Windows host
- [Set Up the On-Prem Agent](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/on-prem-agent/setup.md): Configure and deploy the on-prem agent Docker container for your customers
- [Troubleshooting On-Prem Connections](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/connections/on-prem-agent/troubleshooting.md): Some tips for troubleshooting on-prem connections
- [Data Sources](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/data-sources.md): Create dynamic config variables in the config wizard that fetch data from external APIs
- [Code Component Data Sources](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/data-sources/code-component-data-sources.md): Learn how to use the code component to fetch data from a third-party API to present in the config wizard
- [Debugging JSON Forms Locally](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/data-sources/debugging.md): Debug a JSON Forms data source that is throwing an error by running it in your IDE
- [Salesforce Field Mapper](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/data-sources/field-mapping/salesforce-field-mapper.md): Build a data source using JSON forms and an existing Salesforce connection to perform field mapping from SFDC to your application

- [Renderers Reference](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/data-sources/json-forms/reference/renderers.md): Reference for the built-in JSON Forms renderers Prismatic uses in the configuration wizard, including how schema types map to input controls and what options each renderer accepts.

#### Triggers

- [Triggers Overview](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers.md): Learn about the different ways to trigger your integrations
- [App Event Triggers](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/app-events.md): Listen to events in external apps
- [Cross-Flow Trigger](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/cross-flow.md): Call other flows within the same integration
- [Endpoint Configuration](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/endpoint-configuration.md): You can choose to assign a unique webhook URL to each flow, have each instance share an endpoint, or share an endpoint for all instances of an integration
- [Flow Concurrency & FIFO](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/fifo-queue.md): Manage how your flows behave when multiple invocations occur simultaneously.
- [Listening Mode](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/listening-mode.md): Use listening mode to test webhooks in the integration designer
- [Management Triggers](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/management.md): Run certain flows of your integration when an instance is created or removed
- [Schedule Triggers](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/schedule.md): You can run integrations on a schedule
- [Single-Endpoint Webhook Integrations](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/single-endpoint-webhook-integrations.md): Some apps, like Slack, Dropbox or Hubspot, require a single endpoint to be configured for all events. This guide explains how to route events to the correct instance in such cases.
- [Universal Webhook Trigger](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/universal-webhook.md): The universal webhook trigger when a connector does not have a dedicated built-in trigger
- [Using Shared Webhooks and Preprocess Flows](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/using-shared-webhooks-and-preprocess-flows.md): Learn how to use a shared webhook endpoint for multiple customers, and route webhook invocations to specific customers and flows.
- [What is a Webhook?](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/webhook.md): Learn about webhooks and how to use them.
- [Custom HMAC Trigger](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/webhook/custom-hmac-trigger.md): How to build a custom HMAC trigger
- [Sending data to webhook triggers](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/webhook/sending-data.md): You can send several types of data to a webhook endpoint
- [Synchronous and Asynchronous Invocations](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/webhook/synchronous-and-asynchronous.md): A webhook can be invoked synchronously or asynchronously
- [What is HMAC?](https://prismatic.io/docs/integrations/triggers/webhook/what-is-hmac.md): Here's a simple way to ensure that only authorized systems can send data to webhook endpoints.

- [Xero Connector](https://prismatic.io/docs/components/xero.md): Manage invoices, items, accounts, payments, and more in Xero.. Learn more about using Prismatic's Xero component.
- [Yoti Sign Connector](https://prismatic.io/docs/components/yoti-sign.md): Yoti Sign is a digital identity and e-signature solution that allows users to verify their identity and sign documents electronically and securely.. Learn more about using Prismatic's Yoti Sign component.
- [Zendesk Connector](https://prismatic.io/docs/components/zendesk.md): Manage tickets and users in Zendesk.. Learn more about using Prismatic's Zendesk component.
- [Zendesk Sell Connector](https://prismatic.io/docs/components/zendesk-sell.md): Manage leads, contacts, and deals in Zendesk Sell.. Learn more about using Prismatic's Zendesk Sell component.
- [Zip Connector](https://prismatic.io/docs/components/zip.md): Provides utility methods for working with zip files. Learn more about using Prismatic's Zip component.
- [Zoho Connector](https://prismatic.io/docs/components/zoho.md): Manage records, contacts, and transactions in Zoho CRM and Books. Learn more about using Prismatic's Zoho component.
- [Zoom Connector](https://prismatic.io/docs/components/zoom.md): Manage meetings, recordings, users, and webinars in Zoom.. Learn more about using Prismatic's Zoom component.

## API Reference

> Comprehensive reference for Prismatic's GraphQL-based API, including schema details and usage examples.

- [Prismatic's API Overview](https://prismatic.io/docs/api.md): Learn about Prismatic's GraphQL API
- [Authentication](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/authentication.md): Authenticate with Prismatic's GraphQL API
- [Authentication in a CI/CD System](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/ci-cd-system.md): Query Prismatic's GraphQL API from a CI/CD system
- [Creating Instances Programmatically](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/common-queries/creating-instances.md): Create instances programmatically using Prismatic's GraphQL API
- [Fetching Logs Programmatically](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/common-queries/fetching-logs.md): Fetch logs programmatically using Prismatic's GraphQL API
- [Fetching Step Results Programmatically](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/common-queries/fetching-step-results.md): Fetch step results programmatically using Prismatic's GraphQL API
- [Managing Customers Programmatically](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/common-queries/managing-customers.md): Manage customers programmatically using Prismatic's GraphQL API
- [Updating Config Variables Programmatically](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/common-queries/updating-config-variables.md): Update config variables of instances programmatically using Prismatic's GraphQL API
- [Determining Webhook URLs Programmatically](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/common-queries/webhook-urls.md): Fetch webhook URLs and instances from webhook URLs programmatically
- [Querying Prismatic's API from an HTTP Client](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/get-started/querying-with-http-client.md): Query Prismatic's GraphQL API from an HTTP client
- [Query Prismatic's API with Node.js](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/get-started/querying-with-nodejs.md): Query Prismatic's GraphQL API from a Node.js script
- [Query Prismatic's API with Python](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/get-started/querying-with-python.md): Query Prismatic's GraphQL API from a Python script
- [Using the GraphiQL Explorer](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/get-started/using-prismatic-graphql-explorer.md): Test GraphQL queries with Prismatic's GraphQL explorer
- [GitHub Actions](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/github-actions.md): Learn how to use GitHub Actions to publish custom components and integrations
- [Pagination with Prismatic's API](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/pagination.md): Learn how to paginate through results in Prismatic's GraphQL API
- [Prismatic API Queries and Mutations](https://prismatic.io/docs/api/queries-and-mutations.md): Queries and mutations using Prismatic's GraphQL API

Platform overview

# 

B2B Integration Platform Built for Scale

Prismatic's core platform handles authentication, monitoring, scaling, and security while AI-enabled code-native development, low-code tools, and embedded experiences give you flexible ways to build.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)[Watch a demo video](/demo-video-wcr/)

Jump to

OverviewBuildDeployManageConnectorsDev Experience

The Prismatic Platform

## 

Infrastructure with flexibility and scale

Prismatic is purpose-built for B2B software companies, not retrofitted from internal IT tools. The platform combines enterprise-tested infrastructure with flexible, AI-enabled build experiences that empower your entire team, from devs who want to write code to end-users who need visual tools.

### Core infrastructure

The foundation that handles everything that breaks at scale: authentication, multi-tenant deployment, monitoring, security, and CI/CD.

Learn more

### Flexible build experiences

Code-native TypeScript with AI agents, low-code designer, embedded workflow builder, and 150+ pre-built components.

Learn more

### Deploy & manage tools

Customer-specific configuration, embedded marketplace, self-serve debugging, and detailed monitoring for your teams.

Learn more

Build

### 

Build any integration 10x faster with AI

Prismatic gives your team multiple ways to build, from full-code TypeScript to low-code visual tools, all accelerated by AI. Choose the approach that fits your team's needs.

Code-native integrations

Write code in your IDE, use AI agents through our MCP dev server, and deploy from your terminal. Everything developers love (type safety, local testing, version control) with none of the low-code limitations.

[Learn More about how we compare](/platform/how-we-compare/)

Low-code integration designer

Drag-and-drop interface that empowers anyone to build and modify integrations. 190+ pre-built components make it easy to handle common patterns without writing code.

[Learn more about low code integration designer](/platform/low-code-integration-designer/)

Embedded workflow builder

Embed Prismatic's builder directly into your product so customers can create their own integrations and automations. Reduce engineering lift and increase product stickiness.

[Learn more about code native integrations](/platform/code-native-integrations/)

DEPLOY

### 

Build once, deploy to thousands

The hard part isn't building integrations. It's deploying them at scale with customer-specific auth, config, and requirements. Prismatic handles this complexity for you.

Integration marketplace

Embed a marketplace directly in your product where customers discover, activate, and configure integrations themselves. No engineering involvement required.

[Learn More about launch an integration marketplace](/solutions/launch-an-integration-marketplace/)

Configuration and deployment tools

Deploy integrations with customer-specific auth, configuration, and monitoring. Give Customer Success teams the tools to deploy without engineering.

[Learn more about configuration deployment tools](/platform/configuration-deployment-tools/)

MANAGE

### 

Proactive monitoring at scale

Give customers and your team the visibility to troubleshoot issues fast. Self-serve logs reduce support burden while detailed monitoring keeps integrations running reliably.

Customer self-serve support tools

Give customers direct access to integration logs and execution history so they can troubleshoot issues themselves. Reduces support tickets while improving satisfaction.

[Learn more about customer self serve support tools](/platform/customer-self-serve-support-tools/)

Monitoring and management tools

Detailed execution logs, alerting dashboards, and streaming to tools like Datadog, New Relic, and PagerDuty. Everything your team needs for first-class integration support.

[Learn more about monitoring management tools](/platform/monitoring-management-tools/)

Large data syncs at a glance

See high-volume syncs roll up as a single execution with batch-level progress, success counts, and failure tracking. Makes monitoring and troubleshooting large data syncs as straightforward as any other integration.

[Learn more about bulk data sync](/docs/integrations/common-patterns/bulk-data-sync/)

Extensible connector library

## 

Built-in and custom API connectors

Easily connect to third-party applications with Prismatic’s built-in API connectors. Auth is fully handled.

Integrate with any product your customers use, no matter how niche. Code robust custom connectors using our powerful SDK.

[Explore connectors](/connectors/)[Read SDK Docs](/docs/custom-components/writing-custom-components/)

Developer Experience

## 

Built for how devs actually work

Most integration platforms force developers into rigid low-code tools that slow them down. Prismatic works the way developers want to work: write code in your IDE, use your existing tools, and ship through your CI/CD pipeline.

[See Docs](/docs/)

What makes Prismatic different

Write code in your IDE

Build integrations in TypeScript using VS Code or your preferred IDE, not in a browser

AI-powered development

MCP server support for Claude, Cursor, and other coding agents

Infrastructure handled

No maintaining OAuth flows, retry logic, or deployment systems

Local testing and deployment

Test locally, then deploy through your CI/CD pipeline

Fully scriptable platform

CLI and API for everything, version control for all integrations

No low-code limitations

Full flexibility to build any integration your customers need

## 

Common questions

What is a B2B integration platform?

A B2B integration platform enables a software company to build and deliver integrations between its product and the other applications its customers use. 

Unlike traditional integration platforms designed for internal automation, B2B integration platforms are purpose-built to handle the unique challenges of customer-facing integrations at scale.

These platforms handle the infrastructure pieces that typically consume development resources: authentication across multiple customers, multi-tenant deployment, monitoring, error handling, and security. They provide both the building tools (low-code designers, code-native development environments, pre-built connectors) and the deployment tools (embedded marketplaces and configuration wizards) needed to deliver integrations as a first-class product feature.

The key difference is the deployment model. With a B2B integration platform, you build an integration once and deploy it to thousands of customers, each with their own configuration and credentials. This approach is fundamentally different from building one-off integrations for internal use or creating separate integrations for each customer.

How does a B2B integration platform differ from traditional iPaaS?

Which companies benefit most from a B2B integration platform?

Can a B2B integration platform handle API and data integrations?

How does a B2B integration platform ensure data security?

How does an embedded integration platform scale as my business grows?

Build fast

# 

Low-Code Integration Designer

Prismatic's low-code integration designer is a visual canvas for B2B SaaS teams that need to build, test, and deploy customer integrations quickly (using pre-built connectors and drag-and-drop logic) without writing infrastructure code or waiting on a dev for every new request.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)[Watch a demo video](/demo-video-wcr/)

Fast and Flexible

## 

Build integrations as fast as your customers need them

Stop choosing which integrations to build based on deal size.

Our visual designer lets your team ship integrations in hours, whether it's a simple data sync or complex workflow automation. Build once, deploy to hundreds of customers.

[Build in low-code](/docs/integrations/)

Built-in and custom connectors

## 

Connect to everything your customers use

Start with our extensive library of pre-built connectors to popular apps. OAuth flows, retry logic, and error handling come standard.

Need something custom? Extend with TypeScript or use our HTTP connector to connect to any API, while we handle the infrastructure that breaks at scale.

[Explore connectors](/connectors/)

Configurable integrations

## 

Build once, deploy to many customers

Stop rebuilding the same integration for every customer. Create configurations that adapt to each customer's unique requirements.

Let customers activate their integrations in minutes through your embedded marketplace with no tickets and no delays.

[See integration marketplace](/solutions/launch-an-integration-marketplace/)

Testing framework

## 

Deploy with confidence at any scale

Test integrations in real-time as you build. Debug with detailed execution logs, monitor performance across all tenants, and iterate without breaking production.

Our infrastructure handles retry logic, queuing, and scaling automatically, so you ship reliable integrations from day one.

[Read the docs](/docs/integrations/low-code-integration-designer/testing/)

Dev-friendly capabilities

## 

Built for how modern dev teams actually work

When devs get involved with Prismatic’s low-code, they love what they find.

  * Extend with TypeScript when visual building isn't enough.

  * Drop custom code blocks directly into any workflow.

  * Automate everything via CLI and API for CI/CD pipelines.

  * Version control integrations alongside your codebase.

  * Switch to code-native development when complexity demands it.




[See the platform](/platform/)

We are pleased to mention our partnership with Prismatic when discussing system integration with prospects, customers, and other solution providers.

Jeff Holmes

Manager, Engineering

Both technical and non-technical team members use our visual designer. Product managers and solutions engineers can handle most integration builds, while developers can jump in for complex logic or custom components. Many teams report a 95% reduction in engineering time spent on integrations.

# Code-native integrations

Source: https://prismatic.io/platform/code-native-integrations/

[We've open-sourced our connectors. Find out why!](/blog/connectors-are-the-commodity-embedded-ipaas/)

[](/)

  * Platform
  * Solutions
  * Resources
  * [Pricing](/pricing/)



[Login](https://app.prismatic.io)

[Start a free trial](/free-trial/)[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)

Build

# 

Code-Native Integrations

Prismatic's code-native approach lets B2B SaaS developers write integrations in TypeScript with their own IDEs – using their existing tools, AI copilots, and CI/CD pipeline – while Prismatic's embedded iPaaS handles the deployment, configuration, and multi-tenant infrastructure that would otherwise be a separate engineering project.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)[Watch a demo video](/demo-video-wcr/)

The developer's choice

## 

Build integrations the way developers actually work

Low-code works for some scenarios. But when you need speed, flexibility, or complexity, developers want to write code.

Code-native gives you the full power of TypeScript with AI assistance, while Prismatic's platform handles all the infrastructure that slows teams down.

[Read the docs](/docs/code-native-integrations/)[Explore our MCP dev server](/solutions/build-integrations-faster-with-ai/)

TypeScript in any IDE

## 

Keep your tools and processes

The last thing you need is something outside your existing toolchain. Code integrations using modern TypeScript in your preferred IDE.

Use our VS Code extension to bring Prismatic's capabilities directly in your environment. Take advantage of your current setup – linters, AI copilots, CI/CD pipeline. Everything is scriptable through the Prismatic CLI and API.

Ultimate flexibility

## 

Build any integration, the way you want

Write whatever code you need to build any integration your customers require. Use npm packages, call external APIs, or implement complex business logic, completely free of low-code constraints. From complex ERP systems to proprietary internal tools, there are no limitations.

[Learn more about flexibility](/solutions/build-integrations-faster-with-ai/)

Accelerate development

## 

Save time with custom and built-in connectors

No need to reinvent the wheel. Call Prismatic’s built-in connectors or your custom connectors to take advantage of auth, triggers, and actions that have already been built.

Import connectors as TypeScript functions with automatic auth handling and full type safety. Use them when you need them, or call APIs directly when you don't.

[Explore connectors](/connectors/)

Purpose-built infrastructure

## 

Code the integration, let our platform handle the rest

Coding integrations is just the first step. Prismatic's purpose-built infrastructure handles configuration, deployment, monitoring, and scaling across your entire customer base.

Developers build once and define the config interface. Non-technical teams can then deploy to individual customers using visual wizards. No code changes needed.

[Platform overview](/platform/)

## 

Common questions

Can we use code-native integrations alongside low-code integrations?

Absolutely. Many teams use code-native for complex integrations and low-code for simpler ones. Both deploy to the same infrastructure and share the same components, connectors, and deployment tools. You can even convert low-code integrations to code-native when complexity increases.

How do non-technical teams deploy code-native integrations?

Can we use our existing CI/CD pipeline?

What happens when we need to update an integration?

Do code-native integrations work with the embedded marketplace?

Can we migrate existing integrations to code-native?

How does pricing work for code-native integrations?

# Embedded workflow builder

Source: https://prismatic.io/platform/embedded-workflow-builder/

[We've open-sourced our connectors. Find out why!](/blog/connectors-are-the-commodity-embedded-ipaas/)

[](/)

  * Platform
  * Solutions
  * Resources
  * [Pricing](/pricing/)



[Login](https://app.prismatic.io)

[Start a free trial](/free-trial/)[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)

Build

# 

Embedded Workflow Builder

Prismatic's embedded workflow builder is a white-labeled, low-code automation tool that B2B SaaS teams enable directly inside their products, letting their customers build, customize, and run their own integration workflows without engineering help. 

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)[Start a free trial](/free-trial/)

[AI Copilot for embedded workflow builder](/blog/ai-copilot-for-embedded-workflow-builder-early-access/)

## 

AI Copilot drives success

AI Copilot brings natural language into your embedded product experience. Customers describe what they need, watch it take shape on the canvas in real time, and stay in control throughout.

### [Match customers' skillsNot every customer is a power user. AI Copilot removes the learning curve by letting users describe workflow goals in plain language instead of manually configuring each step. Learn more](/blog/ai-copilot-for-embedded-workflow-builder-early-access/)

### [Reduce time to valueWhen your customers get stuck mid-build, AI Copilot gets them moving again. Users can invoke it at any point: start from scratch, extend an existing flow, or refine step by step.Learn more](/blog/ai-copilot-for-embedded-workflow-builder-early-access/)

### [Delight enterprise customersAI Copilot runs natively inside your product. That means workflow building stays within your security and compliance boundaries – a critical requirement for enterprise buyers. Learn more ](/blog/ai-copilot-for-embedded-workflow-builder-early-access/)

Self-serve automation for your customers

## 

Benefits of embedded workflow builder for SaaS products

  * Customers define workflows that connect your product to their other tools

  * Win and retain enterprise accounts with self-service capabilities

  * Reduce one-off requests by letting customers configure their own workflows

  * Increase stickiness as customers embed critical processes in your product




[Read the docs](/docs/embed/workflow-builder/)

Pre-built and custom components

## 

Provide low-code building blocks

Your customers define workflows using Prismatic's library of drag-and-drop API connectors and logic components, all embedded in your product.

Add custom components that connect to your product's API and the tools specific to your industry. You control which components are available to customers, ensuring they can build the workflows they need while staying within your governance policies.

[Explore connectors](/connectors/)

Complete white-labeling

## 

Provide a seamless experience

Prismatic's theming system allows the embedded workflow builder to match your product's design, from colors and fonts to custom branding.

You get a workflow builder without building it yourself. Your customers get a native experience without knowing Prismatic exists.

## 

Common questions

Can non-technical users really build integrations with the embedded workflow builder?

Yes. The visual, drag-and-drop interface is designed for business users, not developers. Your customers can connect systems, set up triggers, map data, and create complex workflows without writing code. Most users are building their first automation within minutes.

How much control do I have over what customers can build?

What happens when a customer's workflow breaks?

How does pricing work for customer-built workflows?

Can the embedded builder work with our existing integrations?

# AI for integrations

Source: https://prismatic.io/platform/ai-for-integrations/

[We've open-sourced our connectors. Find out why!](/blog/connectors-are-the-commodity-embedded-ipaas/)

[](/)

  * Platform
  * Solutions
  * Resources
  * [Pricing](/pricing/)



[Login](https://app.prismatic.io)

[Start a free trial](/free-trial/)[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)

AI-powered platform

# 

A Platform Built for the AI Era

Prismatic is an embedded iPaaS for B2B SaaS teams that delivers AI on both sides of the integration: developer-side tooling that accelerates how you build, and run-time infrastructure that lets AI agents invoke those integrations as reliable, production-ready workflows.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)[Watch a demo video](/demo-video-wcr/)

The Next Evolution

## 

Prismatic + AI

As the leading embedded iPaaS, Prismatic delivers AI capabilities in two key areas: accelerating how you build integrations and enabling your customers to leverage AI agents with your integrations.

Developers build integrations faster with AI coding assistants in their IDE using our MCP dev server. Your customers' AI agents invoke complete integration workflows via the Prismatic MCP flow server. And teams add intelligence directly into integrations with built-in AI connectors.

This is purpose-built infrastructure for AI-powered integrations, not retrofitted functionality.

[Learn more about prismatic ai next evolution](/blog/prismatic-ai-next-evolution/)

Build fast with AI assistance

## 

Build integrations with AI-assisted tools

Our MCP dev server connects AI coding assistants like Claude or Cursor directly to Prismatic, enabling context-aware development in your IDE.

And Prismatic Skills is a Claude Code plugin that gives Claude deep, specialized knowledge of the Prismatic platform.

It turns Claude from a general-purpose coding assistant into an integration specialist that can build integrations, create custom connectors, scaffold embedded experiences, and operate your Prismatic environment, all from your editor.

[Explore MCP dev server](/solutions/build-integrations-faster-with-ai/)[Explore Prismatic Skills](/solutions/build-integrations-with-claude/)

Deploy AI-accessible workflows

## 

Expose integrations as AI tools

The Prismatic MCP flow server exposes your integration workflows as structured tools that AI agents can discover and invoke.

Instead of AI agents making unreliable chains of individual API calls, they invoke complete flows where you've defined the exact execution order, authentication, error handling, and business logic. Your customers get deterministic, production-grade workflows that their AI agents can use confidently.

This gives you control over how AI agents interact with integrations while providing the intelligence your customers expect.

[Explore MCP flow server](/solutions/add-ai-capabilities-to-integrations/)

Intelligence in your workflows

## 

Add AI capabilities to integration logic

Beyond development acceleration and agent connectivity, add intelligence directly into your integration workflows.

Use built-in connectors for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and other AI services. Create agent flows that make decisions and trigger actions autonomously. Combine AI automation with human-in-the-loop approval for critical workflows. Or bring your own AI with frameworks like LangChain, CrewAI, and AutoGen.

Common use cases include data enrichment, smart extraction, AI routing and classification, and conversational interfaces.

[Explore AI connectors](/connectors/)

## 

Common questions

What's the difference between the MCP dev server and MCP flow server?

Prism MCP dev server runs in your IDE and accelerates development by connecting AI coding assistants to Prismatic's platform. Prismatic MCP flow server runs in production and exposes your deployed integrations as tools that your customers' AI agents can invoke.

Do I need to use MCP to build AI-powered integrations?

How do agent flows differ from LLM-orchestrated integrations not using MCP?

What AI services and models does Prismatic support?

How is my data secured when using AI features?

Are AI features available now?

# Monitoring & management tools

Source: https://prismatic.io/platform/monitoring-management-tools/

[We've open-sourced our connectors. Find out why!](/blog/connectors-are-the-commodity-embedded-ipaas/)

[](/)

Manage

# 

Embedded Integration Monitoring and Management Tools

Prismatic's monitoring and management tools give B2B SaaS teams cross-customer visibility into every deployed integration (execution status, version, configuration, logs, and alerts) streamed directly to the observability platforms they already use.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)[Watch a demo video](/demo-video-wcr/)

Built for scale

## 

Stop building integration infrastructure

Managing integrations in production becomes a nightmare at scale. And building the tooling to do it well is a whole separate dev project. Prismatic gives you enterprise-tested monitoring and management tools so your team can focus on integrations, not infrastructure.

[Learn more about reducing integration workload for your engineering team](/blog/reducing-integration-workload-for-your-engineering-team/)

Full visibility

## 

Know the status of every customer's integrations

See everything at a glance: what integrations each customer has deployed, what versions they're running, how they're configured, current status, and when they last executed. Filter across all customers or drill into a specific instance.

Reliable infrastructure

## 

Fewer issues, faster resolution

Integrations are only as stable as the platform they run on. Prismatic handles retry logic, queuing, and scaling automatically, preventing the issues that typically cause production headaches.

Logging and alerting

## 

Get notified instantly, troubleshoot fast

onfigure alerts for failed executions, slow runs, or unexpected disabled states. Send those alerts via Pager Duty, Slack, or another tool. Dig into detailed execution logs to pinpoint issues. Stream detailed logs to Datadog, New Relic, or another logging platform.

[Read the docs](/docs/monitor-instances/logging/streaming-logs-externally/)

## 

Common questions

What is an integration monitoring tool and why do I need one?

An integration monitoring tool tracks the health and performance of your integrations in production, alerting you when issues occur so you can address them right away. Without monitoring, you might not know about integration failures until a customer calls, which may be hours after the problem started. Prismatic's monitoring tools provide comprehensive visibility into integration execution across your entire customer base, showing you which integrations are running, which have failed, execution times, and detailed logs for troubleshooting. 

You can configure alerts triggered by specific conditions, such as execution failures, elevated error logs, or executions that take longer than expected. These alerts notify the right people on your team via email, SMS, or webhooks to systems like Slack or PagerDuty. This approach prevents constant firefighting, reduces customer frustration, and ensures your support team can identify and resolve issues before they escalate.

How does Prismatic send alerts and logs to my existing tools?

Can I scale integration management as my business grows?

Is Prismatic suitable for teams with limited technical resources?

# Launch an integration marketplace

Source: https://prismatic.io/solutions/launch-an-integration-marketplace/

Integration Marketplace

# 

Launch an Integration Marketplace

Prismatic's embedded marketplace is a white-labeled, self-serve integration hub that B2B SaaS teams place directly inside their products – so customers can browse, authenticate, configure, and manage their own integrations without opening a support ticket.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)[Watch a demo video](/free-trial/)

Better discoverability

## 

Make integrations accessible

Display your integrations in a branded marketplace that matches your product's look and feel. Users can browse and discover integrations for their favorite apps without leaving your product.

Make integrations easy to find, increase adoption, and create product stickiness.

Easy activation

## 

Connect to third-party apps in a few clicks

Reduce support tickets asking, "How do I connect integrations?” Users can find the integration they want and safely authenticate in just a few clicks, so it's live in your product.

[](/connectors/)

Configuration wizard

## 

User-level configuration made easy

Build powerful and intuitive configuration experiences, from simple booleans to complex field mapping. Users configure integrations themselves while your team maintains control over the logic.

Integration management

## 

Let users manage their own integrations

Users control their integrations directly from the marketplace. They can view status, update configurations, or disconnect when needed. Your team stays focused on your product. 

[Read the docs](/docs/integrations/embedded-marketplace/)

Embedding options

## 

Embed with code or build your own

Embed the marketplace in your product as an iframe with custom theming, colors, and translations. Or use Prismatic's API to build a completely custom experience that aligns with your product's look and feel.

[Learn how](/docs/embedding-marketplace)

## 

Common questions

Can I build a custom marketplace and still use Prismatic?

Yes. Build a custom UX against Prismatic's API, or embed our iframe marketplace and theme it to match your brand. Both options use Prismatic's infrastructure to deliver integrations to your customers.

How does authentication work?

Can different customers configure the same integration differently?

What happens when a third-party API changes? 

Do my customers need my help to manage their integrations?

# 

The White Label Integration Platform for B2B SaaS Products

Launch powerful native integrations to the other products your customers use with Prismatic's embedded integration platform.

Trusted by engineering teams from Fortune 500s to startups

## 

Faster integration delivery means faster everything

Providing integrations to your customers takes a ton of engineering time, derails your product roadmap, and slows sales and onboarding. And it only gets harder at scale.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)[Start a free trial](/free-trial/)

## 

What's the difference between Prismatic and a traditional integration platform?

| | Traditional iPaaS  
---|---|---  
Platform purpose| SaaS products providing native integrations for customers| Enterprises connecting their own internal applications  
Low-code integration designer| |   
Connectors to common SaaS applications| |   
Build integrations once, deploy across customers| |   
Configurable integrations to meet customer-specific needs| |   
Self-serve integration marketplace embedded in your apps| |   
Deployment and support tooling for multiple customers| |   
Fits software teams' existing infrastructure and processes| |   
  
  *   * Platform purpose

SaaS products providing native integrations for customers

  * Low-code integration designer

  * Connectors to common SaaS applications

  * Build integrations once, deploy across customers

  * Configurable integrations to meet customer-specific needs

  * Self-serve integration marketplace embedded in your apps

  * Deployment and support tooling for multiple customers

  * Fits software teams' existing infrastructure and processes



  * Traditional iPaaS
  * Platform purpose

Enterprises connecting their own internal applications

  * Low-code integration designer

  * Connectors to common SaaS applications

  * Build integrations once, deploy across customers

  * Configurable integrations to meet customer-specific needs

  * Self-serve integration marketplace embedded in your apps

  * Deployment and support tooling for multiple customers

  * Fits software teams' existing infrastructure and processes




## 

Scale your integration strategy fast

Flexible Integration Designer

## Combine pre-built and custom connectors to power integrations

The intuitive low-code designer empowers non-devs to create integrations by assembling connectors and other components.

And, devs can write code with our Node.js SDK to create custom connectors to any third-party app your customers use.

white label integration hub

## Create a powerful self-serve integration experience for your customers

Embed Prismatic's self-serve integration marketplace in your app to help customers explore and discover your integrations. Users can self-activate integrations with just a few clicks to connect their third-party apps & choose config options - without needing to involve your team.

# Add AI capabilities to integrations

Source: https://prismatic.io/solutions/add-ai-capabilities-to-integrations/

[We've open-sourced our connectors. Find out why!](/blog/connectors-are-the-commodity-embedded-ipaas/)

[](/)

  * Platform
  * Solutions
  * Resources
  * [Pricing](/pricing/)



[Login](https://app.prismatic.io)

[Start a free trial](/free-trial/)[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)

AI-POWERED WORKFLOWS

# 

Add AI Capabilities to Integrations

Prismatic's LLM connectors let B2B SaaS teams drop pre-built components for OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, and other AI services directly into integrations – so data can be enriched, classified, summarized, or transformed by AI in real time, without building or managing separate AI infrastructure.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)[Watch a demo video](/demo-video-wcr/)

## 

Embed intelligence in integration workflows

Your customers don't just need to move data between systems, they need to transform it, analyze it, and act on it intelligently with AI-enabled integration workflows that go beyond simple data sync. Prismatic's LLM connectors let you embed AI capabilities directly into integration workflows, giving customers powerful automation without building AI infrastructure.

### Pre-built LLM connectors

Ready-to-use connectors for OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, and other leading AI services. Authentication and API management handled automatically.

### Powerful workflow integration

Drop AI connectors into integration workflows to enrich CRM data, classify support tickets, generate summaries, extract insights, all in real-time as data flows through your integrations.

### Customer-specific AI configuration

Each customer can use their own AI service credentials or leverage shared accounts. Multi-tenant isolation ensures data security and proper cost attribution.

PLUG-AND-PLAY AI

## 

AI-enabled workflows for enterprise integrations

Build integrations that do more than just sync data. Use LLM connectors to analyze customer sentiment, generate personalized content, extract structured data from documents, classify and route information, all within your existing integration workflows. No need to build AI infrastructure or manage API keys. Drop an LLM component into your flow, configure the prompt, and deploy. Your customers get intelligent automation without the complexity.

[Explore LLM connectors](/connectors/)

## 

Supported AI services and connectors

Prismatic provides pre-built connectors for major AI services, or build custom connectors for specialized models. Your customers get the flexibility to use the AI providers that fit their requirements and budgets.

**Supported AI services**

  * OpenAI

  * Anthropic Claude

  * Google Gemini

  * Azure OpenAI

  * Custom models via API

  * And more




[View all AI connectors](/connectors/)

Developer benefits

## 

Enterprise-ready AI workflows

AI-powered integrations need the same reliability, security, and scalability as any production integration. Prismatic provides the infrastructure to deploy AI workflows at scale with proper authentication, error handling, and monitoring.

### Multi-tenant credential management

Each customer can use their own AI service API keys, or you can provide shared credentials. Full isolation and cost attribution.

### Error handling and retries

Built-in retry logic and graceful degradation when AI services are unavailable or rate-limited.

### Prompt management

Version-controlled prompts that can be updated without redeploying integrations. Test and refine AI behavior safely.

### Full observability

Monitor AI component performance, token usage, and costs. Debug with complete execution logs.

### Rate limiting and cost controls

Set guardrails to prevent runaway costs. Monitor and alert on AI service usage per customer.

### Compliance and security

SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, and HIPAA compliant infrastructure ensures AI workflows meet enterprise security standards.

### Multi-tenant credential management

### Error handling and retries

### Prompt management

### Full observability

### Rate limiting and cost controls

### Compliance and security

## 

Common questions

How do LLM connectors work in Prismatic?

LLM connectors are components you add to integration workflows, just like any other connector. Configure the AI service, set up your prompt, and the component handles API calls, authentication, and response parsing automatically.

Do customers need their own AI service API keys?

What AI capabilities can I add to integrations?

How do I control AI costs?

Can I use my own custom AI models?

How is data security handled?

Get a Demo

# 

Make Integrations Work Correctly

Prismatic is an embedded iPaaS for B2B SaaS developers who want to build integrations in TypeScript with AI assistants inside their own IDEs without also having to build and maintain the auth, multi-tenant deployment, monitoring, and scaling infrastructure that production integrations require.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)[Start a free trial](/free-trial/)

Trusted by engineering teams from Fortune 500s to startups

## 

AI that enables core product focus

AI rulesets and an MCP dev server to speed up building. No more time-consuming one-off integration builds, no infrastructure or UI to stand up, no more dev cycle sacrifices.

## 

Build integrations like you build software

Build integrations in code in your IDE with all the tools you already know. Tie into your SDLC with alert monitoring, log streaming, version control, security, and scalability – out of the box.

## 

Hand off support to customer-facing teams

No longer must you dig through the black box of integrations. Customer-facing teams access alerts and logs to troubleshoot in real-time without involving engineering.

## Ready to level up your integration strategy? 

Our B2B SaaS Integration Strategy Guide is packed with best practices and real-world tactics.

[Read the guide](/guides/integration-strategy-guide/)

# 

Make Integrations Your Competitive Advantage

Prismatic is an embedded iPaaS for B2B SaaS product managers who need integrations to ship faster, stay off the engineering critical path, and deliver a customer experience that makes integrations feel like a native part of the product instead of an afterthought.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)[Start a free trial](/free-trial/)

Trusted by engineering teams from Fortune 500s to startups

## 

Protect dev time

Stop building and maintaining integration infrastructure. Prismatic handles authentication, monitoring, multi-tenant deployment, scaling, security, and compliance so your team can focus on what matters: core product work.

## 

Build integrations 10x faster with AI

Use AI coding assistants with our MCP dev server to generate integration code from natural language. Deploy AI-powered workflows to enrich data and process documents for your customers.

## 

Deliver your ideal integration CX

Power your ideal customer deployment experience: let them self-serve in your product, build their own integrations in a workflow builder, or provide white-glove deployments on their behalf.

# How Prismatic compares

Source: https://prismatic.io/platform/how-we-compare/

Prismatic Embedded iPaaS

# 

Embedded iPaaS Comparison: What Makes Prismatic Different?

Traditional iPaaS platforms were designed for internal automation and retrofitted for B2B use cases. Prismatic was built from day one to help B2B SaaS companies deliver integrations to customers at scale.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)[Watch a demo video](/demo-video-wcr/)

Jump to

OverviewCompareCustomer ReviewsCommon Questions

Built differently

## 

Multi-tenant from the ground up

Traditional iPaaS added multi-tenancy as an afterthought. Prismatic was architected for B2B SaaS; deploy once, configure per customer, and scale across your entire customer-base without performance degradation.

Our founders scaled a B2B SaaS platform with hundreds of integrations serving thousands of customers. They felt this pain. Prismatic is the solution they wish had existed then.

[About us](/about/)

Infrastructure and flexibility

## 

Code-native development meets low-code tooling

Other platforms force you into restrictive low-code tools or rigid frameworks they call "build in code."

Prismatic gives you the best of both worlds. Developers can write TypeScript with full IDE support and AI assistance. Non-technical teams can use the low-code designer. Both leverage the same core platform infrastructure that handles everything that breaks at scale.

[See Docs](/docs/)[Empower non-devs](/solutions/empower-non-devs/)

Real-world complexity

## 

Scales from simple to complex integration needs

Competitor platforms handle basic OAuth and data syncs. Then you hit rate limiting, the need for custom business logic, or webhook reliability, and suddenly you’re on your own.

Prismatic handles real-world complexity providing retry logic, error handling, data transformation, versioning, and everything else that breaks at scale, all out of the box.

[Platform overview](/platform/)

## 

Common Questions

Why shouldn’t we just build integrations in-house?

API calls are just a fraction of an integration. The other key pieces, like authentication, monitoring, error handling, retry logic, versioning, and multi-tenant deployment, are the backbone of what it takes to deliver customer integrations, especially as you scale. Prismatic handles all of this out of the box so your team can focus on shipping integrations, not infrastructure.

How is Prismatic different from traditional iPaaS?

What is the difference between Prismatic and Universal API?

Our team has devs and non-technical people managing integrations. Can both use Prismatic?

Can Prismatic handle our complexity? Or is it just for simple integrations?

# Prismatic vs. Workato

Source: https://prismatic.io/platform/how-we-compare/workato/

[We've open-sourced our connectors. Find out why!](/blog/connectors-are-the-commodity-embedded-ipaas/)

[](/)

  * [Pricing](/pricing/)



[Login](https://app.prismatic.io)

[Start a free trial](/free-trial/)[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)

# 

Prismatic vs Workato:   
Meet Customers Where They Are

Workato was built for IT teams and internal automations. Prismatic is the integration platform purpose-built for B2B software companies to deliver customer-facing integrations faster.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)

Prismatic vs Workato

## 

Overview

Workato was initially designed as an enterprise iPaaS and later adapted for embedded use. Its workflows are optimized for IT departments rather than B2B SaaS customers, forcing you to adapt a clunky UX designed for internal IT teams.

Prismatic is designed for B2B SaaS integrations, helping you align your integration strategy with customer expectations instead of enterprise iPaaS constraints.

Workato limits customization to a subset of Ruby within its low-code environment. Prismatic enables code-native integrations with a TypeScript SDK and access to any npm package, so your team can handle everything from the simplest scenarios to complex business logic and unique customer requirements.

Workato's white-labeling options are limited, so your customers may see the Workato interface rather than your product. Prismatic keeps your brand front and center with a fully white-labeled embedded workflow builder and marketplace, allowing customers to self-serve integrations directly in your product.

# Prismatic vs. Paragon

Source: https://prismatic.io/platform/how-we-compare/paragon/

# 

Prismatic vs Paragon:   
Why Scaling Matters

Paragon's tooling is designed for early-stage needs but lacks the flexibility to support SaaS companies as they scale. Prismatic handles everything that breaks at scale.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)

Prismatic vs Paragon

## 

Overview

Paragon focuses on early-stage companies with basic integration needs. As integration requirements grow more complex, your team will encounter platform limitations. While Paragon claims to support "any third-party API," its custom connector capabilities are significantly limited compared to Prismatic, restricting your team's ability to handle complex, real-world integration scenarios.

Paragon requires that you use its proprietary framework built on low-code blocks, limiting flexibility and access to external libraries. While some npm packages are allowed, usage is restricted to an approved list. Prismatic provides true code-native integrations with a TypeScript SDK and unlimited access to any npm package or TypeScript library.

Paragon lacks an embedded workflow builder, so you’ll need to turn down those one-off integration request or spend precious engineering time to build them. Prismatic's embedded workflow builder enables your customers to configure and manage their integrations in your product, reducing engineering efforts and increasing stickiness.

---|---|---

Embedded integration marketplace| |   
Pre-built connector library| |   
Custom connectors| Full Component SDK| Lightweight wrappers for Rest APIs

# 

Prismatic vs Boomi:   
Why Purpose-Built Matters

Boomi's platform was built for enterprise IT teams managing internal integrations. When your SaaS product needs to deliver customer-facing integrations at scale, Prismatic is built for the task. 

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)

Prismatic vs Boomi

## 

Overview

Boomi is an integration platform built for enterprise companies managing internal IT workflows. Its toolset is optimized for internal users, built around a proprietary development framework. It does not support code-native development, substantially limiting what your dev team can build when integration scenarios get complex.

Boomi also lacks a white-labeled integration marketplace and an embedded workflow builder for your customers. Since it was designed for one-off internal integrations within the enterprise, it lacks the infrastructure to deliver productized, configurable, customer-facing integrations. Your customers have no self-serve way to discover, activate, or manage integrations, and no ability to build custom workflows themselves.

Prismatic is a purpose-built, cloud-native embedded iPaaS that has been wholly focused on B2B SaaS integrations since day one. It provides a first-class UX for non-devs via the low-code designer and for devs via code-native integrations in TypeScript with access to any npm package or external library. A white-labeled marketplace and embedded workflow builder mean your customers get a seamless integration experience that lives inside your product.

# 

Prismatic vs n8n Embedded:   
Why Platform Purpose Matters

n8n Embedded adapts an automation platform originally built for internal workflows. Prismatic is purpose-built for SaaS companies delivering customer-facing integrations as product features.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)

Prismatic vs n8n

## 

Overview

n8n was designed as a developer-first automation platform for internal workflows. While n8n Embedded allows you to embed the n8n workflow builder, its architecture and user experience remain oriented to developer-managed automation rather than customer-facing integrations.

Embedding n8n typically means exposing a generalized workflow editor to your customers or building custom layers to simplify and constrain the experience. As usage scales, your team is responsible for managing tenant isolation, workflow lifecycle, reliability, and operational visibility outside of the platform.

Prismatic was built from day one as an embedded integration platform for SaaS products. It provides the infrastructure, tooling, and customer-facing experiences your team needs to deliver reliable, scalable integrations without repurposing internal automation tooling.

| | N8N  
---|---|---  
Code-native integrations| | Limited (JavaScript nodes only)  
Low-code integration designer| |   
Pre-built connector library| |   
Embedded integration marketplace| |   
Custom connector SDK| Full Node.js environment| Node-based extensibility, no SDK  
Purpose-built for customer-facing integrations| |   
Multi-tenant deployment| |   
Configuration and monitoring tools| | Basic workflow execution logs  
Custom code| Use any npm package or other library|   
Customer-facing integration UX| Purpose-built| Embedded internal workflow editor  
White-labeled experience| |

# 

Prismatic vs In-House: Why Integrations Are Hard

Building customer integrations in-house means B2B SaaS engineering teams must construct and maintain not just the integrations, but the entire integration infrastructure – costing months of delivery time, creating tech debt, and diverting engineers from core product development.

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)

Prismatic vs In-House

## 

Overview

Prismatic's embedded iPaaS is a purpose-built, cloud-native B2B SaaS integration platform best suited for SaaS teams that must create anything from simple to highly complex integrations. It provides a first-class UX for devs (via code-native integrations) and non-devs (via the low-code designer). The platform provides end-to-end integration tooling and infrastructure, including capabilities like AI-powered development and MCP support, so your team can focus on integration logic instead of infrastructure maintenance..

In-house integration development is often highly pragmatic, with teams under a deadline to rapidly deliver core functionality. This approach, while efficient, results in integrations that tend to be heavily customized to specific customer requirements and opaque to non-developers. In addition, customer UX is not usually prioritized over immediate utility, and efforts to build a single, flexible solution for multiple customers are often set aside in favor of a simpler implementation targeting a single customer.

| | In-House  
---|---|---  
Number of devs needed| Initially, 1 to 2. Ongoing, 0 to 1. This is common, but will grow for large orgs.| Initially 1 to N. Ongoing, 1 to N.  
Time-to-market | Weeks or days.| Months.  
Maintenance ownership| Prismatic handles updates, security, and scaling. | 1 or more dedicated DevsOps engineers.  
Costs| Predictable pricing tied to platform subscription and usage. | Substantial up-front dev, DevOps, and cloud costs. Variable ongoing costs (but usually still substantial).   
Reliability| 99.99% uptime per SLAs| Varies from really good to not-so-good.   
Customer self-service| Marketplace (search and activate), dashboards (configure and troubleshoot), and workflow builder (create one-off workflows). | Usually not a priority. Seen as unnecessary in most instances.   
Infrastructure scaling| Autoscaling infrastructure to handle the highs and lows without hiccups. | Varies greatly based on what's been pulled together to support integrations.   
Connector library| Pre-built connectors and a custom connector SDK for building more| Custom, from scratch connectors for each system  
Support tools| Built-in monitoring logging and alerting tools that are accessible to non-devs and customers. | Not usually included, unless as an afterthought. Engineering bears the support load.   
Customization| Provides flexibility (custom connectors, code-native integrations, white-labeling) but encourages standard patterns for efficiency. | Full control, so you can make whatever you wish. But it comes with a steep price and added complexity.  
Productized integrations| Focus on making integrations product features. Build once, deploy many.| Integrations often treated as services (one customer, one custom integration) and not usually optimized for reuse or scalability.  
Security and compliance| Offloads much of this infrastructure by design.| You are directly responsible for building and maintaining auth, establishing compliance, and implementing security.   
Role of non-devs| Can build (low-code designer), deploy, and manage integrations.| Can forward onboarding and support emails to engineering.  
Customer onboarding| You can build new integrations for new customers in short order. | If a new integration is required, development timeframes may significantly delay deal closing.   
Innovation vs tech debt| Frees up engineering to focus on the core product instead of integration infrastructure and support. | Tech debt is a reality of creating custom integrations as fast as you can.   
Churn and retention| Faster onboarding, reliability, and visibility lead to less churn. | When integrations are slow to deploy, unstable, or take much hand-holding, churn risk increases.   
Maintenance load| Much lower since integration infrastructure is pre-built and managed. | As integrations mature, your maintenance burden increases (usually in a linear fashion).   
Usage and metrics| Provides visibility into usage, logs, and performance, enabling better data-driven decisions. | Usually lack accessible metrics for usage, customers, and issues.   
Risk exposure| The platform is outsourced, so you have less control of details, but substantially less risk overall. Compliance with standard frameworks like HIPAA, GDPR, and CJIS are baked in. | You own everything and have complete control, but all the risk is also yours.

Initially, 1 to 2. Ongoing, 0 to 1. This is common, but will grow for large orgs.

  * Time-to-market 

Weeks or days.

  * Maintenance ownership

Prismatic handles updates, security, and scaling. 

  * Costs

Predictable pricing tied to platform subscription and usage. 

  * Reliability

99.99% uptime per SLAs

  * Customer self-service

Marketplace (search and activate), dashboards (configure and troubleshoot), and workflow builder (create one-off workflows). 

  * Infrastructure scaling

Autoscaling infrastructure to handle the highs and lows without hiccups. 

  * Connector library

Pre-built connectors and a custom connector SDK for building more

  * Support tools

Built-in monitoring logging and alerting tools that are accessible to non-devs and customers. 

  * Customization

Provides flexibility (custom connectors, code-native integrations, white-labeling) but encourages standard patterns for efficiency. 

  * Productized integrations

Focus on making integrations product features. Build once, deploy many.

  * Security and compliance

Offloads much of this infrastructure by design.

  * Role of non-devs

Can build (low-code designer), deploy, and manage integrations.

  * Customer onboarding

You can build new integrations for new customers in short order. 

  * Innovation vs tech debt

Frees up engineering to focus on the core product instead of integration infrastructure and support. 

  * Churn and retention

Faster onboarding, reliability, and visibility lead to less churn. 

  * Maintenance load

Much lower since integration infrastructure is pre-built and managed. 

  * Usage and metrics

Provides visibility into usage, logs, and performance, enabling better data-driven decisions. 

  * Risk exposure

The platform is outsourced, so you have less control of details, but substantially less risk overall. Compliance with standard frameworks like HIPAA, GDPR, and CJIS are baked in. 



  * In-House
  * Number of devs needed

Initially 1 to N. Ongoing, 1 to N.

  * Time-to-market 

Months.

  * Maintenance ownership

1 or more dedicated DevsOps engineers.

  * Costs

Substantial up-front dev, DevOps, and cloud costs. Variable ongoing costs (but usually still substantial). 

  * Reliability

Varies from really good to not-so-good. 

  * Customer self-service

Usually not a priority. Seen as unnecessary in most instances. 

  * Infrastructure scaling

Varies greatly based on what's been pulled together to support integrations. 

  * Connector library

Custom, from scratch connectors for each system

  * Support tools

Not usually included, unless as an afterthought. Engineering bears the support load. 

  * Customization

Full control, so you can make whatever you wish. But it comes with a steep price and added complexity.

  * Productized integrations

Integrations often treated as services (one customer, one custom integration) and not usually optimized for reuse or scalability.

  * Security and compliance

You are directly responsible for building and maintaining auth, establishing compliance, and implementing security. 

  * Role of non-devs

Can forward onboarding and support emails to engineering.

  * Customer onboarding

If a new integration is required, development timeframes may significantly delay deal closing. 

  * Innovation vs tech debt

Tech debt is a reality of creating custom integrations as fast as you can. 

  * Churn and retention

When integrations are slow to deploy, unstable, or take much hand-holding, churn risk increases. 

  * Maintenance load

As integrations mature, your maintenance burden increases (usually in a linear fashion). 

  * Usage and metrics

Usually lack accessible metrics for usage, customers, and issues. 

  * Risk exposure

You own everything and have complete control, but all the risk is also yours.

## 

Common Questions

What is an embedded iPaaS? 

An embedded iPaaS is a purpose-built integration platform that a B2B SaaS vendor embeds into its product so customers can connect to their other apps directly from within the UI.

How does building integrations in-house differ from using an embedded iPaas?

Why might an in-house integration strategy fail?

What are key benefits of using an embedded iPaaS like Prismatic?

When might building in-house integrations make sense?

Can I keep my existing in-house integrations if I adopt Prismatic?

How does using Prismatic impact my product roadmap and team focus?

What should I look for when choosing an embedded iPaaS?

How does Prismatic help with customer acquisition, retention, and product differentiation?

# 

Pricing

Build integrations fast, deploy them at scale. Plans designed to grow with any B2B software company, from first integration to enterprise-wide deployment.

## Scale

Everything you need to build integrations faster and deploy them to your growing customer base.

What's included:

  * Build unlimited integrations for unlimited customers

  * Code-native and low-code building tools

  * AI-enabled development with MCP server support

  * Embedded integration marketplace

  * Fully managed authentication

  * Dedicated account manager

  * Volume per-instance pricing




[Schedule my demo](/request-a-demo/)

## Enterprise

Enterprise-scale usage, flexible hosting, and advanced features for every integration scenario.

What's included:

  * Everything in Scale, plus:

  * High execution concurrency limits

  * Private and GovCloud hosting available

  * Embedded workflow builder

  * On-prem connectivity

  * Team member SSO

  * Custom log retention




[Schedule my demo](/request-a-demo/)

## Custom

Enterprise-level functionality with flexible usage limits and pricing for larger deployments.

What's included:

  * Everything in Enterprise, plus:

  * Custom execution concurrency limits

  * Custom instance pricing

  * Custom SLAs




[Schedule my demo](/request-a-demo/)

## 

Common questions

How is Prismatic different from other integration platforms or workflow automation tools

Traditional integration platforms help teams automate their own workflows by connecting the applications used within their business. You might also come across companies that provide a universal API, which allows for basic data syncing but falls short when you need to add business logic or any complexity to your integration. Prismatic is an embedded integration platform that is purpose-built for B2B SaaS companies to help them connect their product to the other applications their customers use. Prismatic is the most efficient way to build, deploy, and manage integrations. We empower everyone on your team with integration tools for devs and non-devs alike. That leads to some key differences, including:

  1. Prismatic integrations can be deployed to multiple customers, each with their own configuration and credentials
  2. Prismatic supports integrating with niche systems that vary widely technically
  3. Prismatic fits smoothly into software teams' existing infrastructure and processes
  4. Prismatic includes an embeddable integration marketplace experience that you can provide to customers



Who uses Prismatic? Engineering teams, or less technical teams?

What kind of integrations can you build using Prismatic?

What is the difference between an "integration" and an "instance"?

What are components, and where can I find a list of available components?

What if a component I need isn't currently available?

How are instances calculated?

What are Prismatic's standard subscription terms?

What is Prismatic's acceptable use policy?

Is Prismatic secure?

What happens if I stop using Prismatic?

What if my Prismatic contract or proposal doesn't match up with the pricing information on this page?

What if I have questions that aren't answered here?

About Us

# 

Making Integrations Easier for B2B SaaS Teams

Prismatic helps B2B SaaS teams make even bigger impacts for users through great integrations and more time for core product innovation. 

[Get a demo](/request-a-demo/)[Start a free trial](/free-trial/)

What Drives Us

## 

Integrations shouldn't be so hard

Our founders previously scaled a B2B SaaS where integrations consumed over 50% of R&D capacity. The process was so time-consuming and painful that they started Prismatic to build the solution they always wished they’d had.

Prismatic helps hundreds of SaaS teams, from startups to Fortune 500s, deliver integrations faster while reclaiming time for core product innovation.

quarters as Embedded iPaaS Leader on G2

in Customer Satisfaction

raised to simplify B2B SaaS integrations

We're leading and innovating

We’re the only embedded iPaaS that empowers both developers and non-developers with first-class tools for the whole build/deploy/manage integration lifecycle. We’re driving the industry forward, and people are noticing.

# Security
